claims.claim: Google's AI content guidance (updated 2026-10-01) says it is critical to manually factcheck and review all AI-generated content for accuracy and trustworthiness before publishing.
claims.sourceName: Google Search Central: Using generative AI content
claims.reason: Last updated 2026-10-01 UTC. "It is critical to manually factcheck and review all AI-generated content for accuracy and trustworthiness before publishing."

claims.claim: Google says this review also applies to metadata that can appear in Search results: <title> elements, meta description elements, structured data, and alternate text for images.
claims.sourceName: Google Search Central: Using generative AI content
claims.reason: "This review also applies to metadata like <title> elements, meta description elements, structured data, and alternate texts for images..."

claims.claim: Google says using generative AI tools to generate many pages without adding value for users may violate its spam policy on scaled content abuse.
claims.sourceName: Google Search Central: Using generative AI content
claims.reason: "using generative AI tools... to generate many pages without adding value for users may violate Google's spam policy on scaled content abuse."

claims.claim: Google's guidance says Search Quality Rater ratings don't directly influence ranking; raters help evaluate the performance of its ranking systems.
claims.sourceName: Google Search Central: Using generative AI content
claims.reason: Raters help "evaluate the performance of our various search ranking systems"; "their ratings don't directly influence ranking."

claims.claim: In a Feb 8, 2023 post, Google said its ranking systems aim to reward original, high-quality content and that it focuses on the quality of content rather than how content is produced.
claims.sourceName: Google Search Central Blog, Feb 8, 2023
claims.reason: Reworded to the source's 'aim to reward' at editor's direction. Post dated Feb 8, 2023; quality-over-production line matches.

claims.claim: Google's 2023 FAQ says appropriate use of AI or automation is not against its guidelines; using it to generate content primarily to manipulate rankings violates its spam policies.
claims.sourceName: Google Search Central Blog, Feb 8, 2023
claims.reason: FAQ: "Appropriate use of AI or automation is not against our guidelines"; using it "primarily to manipulate search rankings" violates spam policies.

claims.claim: Google says using AI doesn't give content any special gains: "It's just content." If it is useful, helpful, original, and satisfies aspects of E-E-A-T, it might do well.
claims.sourceName: Google Search Central Blog, Feb 8, 2023
claims.reason: "Using AI doesn't give content any special gains. It's just content. If it is useful, helpful, original, and satisfies aspects of E-E-A-T, it might do well"

claims.claim: Google defines scaled content abuse as many pages generated primarily to manipulate search rankings and not help users, typically unoriginal and low-value, no matter how it's created.
claims.sourceName: Google Search Central: Spam policies
claims.reason: "many pages are generated for the primary purpose of manipulating search rankings and not helping users... no matter how it's created."

claims.claim: Google's spam policies list using generative AI tools or similar tools to generate many pages without adding value for users as an example of scaled content abuse.
claims.sourceName: Google Search Central: Spam policies
claims.reason: First listed example: "Using generative AI tools or other similar tools to generate many pages without adding value for users".

claims.claim: Google announced the scaled content abuse policy on March 5, 2024, saying it applies whether content is produced through automation, human efforts, or a combination.
claims.sourceName: Google Search Central Blog, Mar 5, 2024
claims.reason: Dated Tuesday, March 5, 2024. Policy applies "no matter whether content is produced through automation, human efforts, or some combination" of the two.

claims.claim: Google's Search Status Dashboard says the August 2026 spam update was released Aug 18, 2026, applies globally and to all languages, and finished rolling out Aug 21, 2026.
claims.sourceName: Google Search Status Dashboard
claims.reason: Aug 18: "Released the August 2026 spam update, which applies globally and to all languages." Aug 21: "The rollout was complete as of August 21, 2026."

claims.claim: Google didn't announce new spam policies or a companion blog post with the August 2026 spam update, according to Search Engine Journal.
claims.sourceName: Search Engine Journal
claims.reason: SEJ: "Google didn't announce any new spam policy types with this rollout" and didn't post a blog article with the release or completion note.

claims.claim: Rater guidelines 4.6.5: scaled content abuse pages are rated Lowest no matter how they're created; if unsure about AI use, raters rate Lowest when they strongly suspect abuse.
claims.sourceName: Google Search Quality Rater Guidelines (Sep 2025)
claims.reason: Reworded to include the 'strongly suspect' condition at editor's direction. Matches 4.6.5.

claims.claim: Rater guidelines 4.6.6: Lowest when all or almost all main content is copied, paraphrased, or AI generated with little to no effort, originality, and added value.
claims.sourceName: Google Search Quality Rater Guidelines (Sep 2025)
claims.reason: Reworded to the 'all or almost all' and three-part test at editor's direction. Matches 4.6.6.

claims.claim: Google says AI or automation disclosures are useful where someone might think "How was this created?" and to consider adding them when it would be reasonably expected.
claims.sourceName: Google Search Central: Creating helpful content
claims.reason: "AI or automation disclosures are useful for content where someone might think 'How was this created?'" Consider adding when reasonably expected.

claims.claim: Google says Merchant Center requires AI-generated images to carry IPTC TrainedAlgorithmicMedia metadata, and AI-generated product titles and descriptions to be labeled as AI-generated.
claims.sourceName: Google Search Central: Using generative AI content
claims.reason: AI images "must contain... IPTC DigitalSourceType TrainedAlgorithmicMedia metadata"; AI product titles and descriptions must be labeled.

claims.claim: Google says it uses a variety of systems, including SpamBrain, that analyze patterns and signals to help identify spam content, however it is produced.
claims.sourceName: Google Search Central Blog, Feb 8, 2023
claims.reason: FAQ: "We have a variety of systems, including SpamBrain, that analyze patterns and signals to help us identify spam content, however it is produced."

claims.claim: Google's John Mueller said what matters is the overall quality published; using AI tools to get started is not a problem on its own, nor a sign content is automatically high quality.
claims.sourceName: Google Search Central Office Hours, June 2024
claims.reason: Mueller: "what matters for us is the overall quality that you end up publishing"; tools "not a problem on its own" but "not a sign" of automatic high quality.

claims.claim: Google's helpful content page, updated October 1, 2026, says using generative AI to produce large amounts of text without manual oversight or curation represents little to no effort.
claims.sourceName: Google Search Central: Creating helpful content
claims.reason: Absent before; Effort: "using generative AI to produce large amounts of text without manual oversight or curation represents little to no effort."

claims.claim: The same update says attribution or giving credit to other sources doesn't replace the need for original effort.
claims.sourceName: Google Search Central: Creating helpful content
claims.reason: Absent before; new under Effort: "Attribution or giving credit to other sources doesn't replace the need for original effort."

claims.claim: The update calls fabricated creator profiles, such as AI-generated headshots, made-up names or false credentials, a form of deception and a signal of a low-quality page.
claims.sourceName: Google Search Central: Creating helpful content
claims.reason: Absent before; new: fabricating creator profiles "is a form of deception"; any deception "is a signal of a low-quality page."

claims.claim: The update says informational content should be factually accurate, and content on YMYL topics must be highly accurate and consistent with expert consensus.
claims.sourceName: Google Search Central: Creating helpful content
claims.reason: Absent before; new Accuracy: info pages "should be factually accurate"; YMYL "must be highly accurate and consistent with established expert consensus."
